title: One-step store
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, $P$ a program, $m$ a memory, and $i,j,a$ integers. Suppose the program at position $pos$ begins with the instruction that stores the word at address $j$ at the address held in $i$, the word at $i$ represents $a$, and $a$ satisfies $-2^W \le 2a < 2^W$. Then one step from $(pos,m)$ reaches program counter $pos+1$ and memory obtained by updating $m$ at address $a$ with the word $m(j)$.
hypotheses_covered: The program at pos begins with store i j
m(i) is the W-bit representation of a
